summary: Deadhorse Airport (SCC) is one of the northernmost public airports in the United States, located on Alaska's North Slope near the Arctic Ocean. It serves as the primary air gateway to the Prudhoe Bay oil fields and surrounding North Slope industrial operations. The airport handles a mix of scheduled commuter flights and charter traffic supporting Alaska's vital petroleum industry.
faqs:
Q: What is Deadhorse Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport mainly serves workers and supplies for the Prudhoe Bay oil fields and other North Slope industrial operations, along with some seasonal tourism traffic.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Deadhorse?
A: Summer (June through August) offers milder temperatures, nearly 24 hours of daylight, and more reliable flight operations. Winter flights face extreme cold, darkness, and frequent weather delays.

Q: Are there commercial flights to Deadhorse?
A: Yes, Alaska Airlines and regional carriers operate scheduled commuter flights, typically from Anchorage and Fairbanks, though schedules are seasonal and weather-dependent.

Q: Is Deadhorse a real town?
A: Deadhorse is a very small industrial community with limited services. Visitors cannot access Prudhoe Bay without authorization from oil companies operating there.
transport_tips: Most travelers arrange ground transportation in advance through oil-company shuttles or pre-booked vans, as Deadhorse has no public transit system. Rental cars are available but limited, and many visitors rely on employer-provided transport. The airport is a short drive from the small Deadhorse settlement and surrounding work camps.
local_tip: Pack layers even in summer—Arctic temperatures can swing dramatically, and the open tundra offers little shelter from wind. Bring any specialty food, medications, or supplies you need, as the local stores have very limited selection and high prices.
